question.problem: Find a tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=2t\,i+(1+{t}^{2})\,j+{t}^{3}\,k$ at the point $P(2,2,1).$
question.worked_solution:
The point $P(2,2,1)$ is at the tip of $r(t)$ for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t.$  At this point,  the vector ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})$ is tangent to the curve.

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to $P.$ We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k \\ 2t\,i+(1+{t}^{2})\,j+{t}^{3}\,k & =2\,i+2\,j+\,k,\end{aligned}
$$

and equating the coefficients of $i,j,$ and $k$ yields the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2t=2 \\ 1+{t}^{2}=2 \\ {t}^{3}=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get $t=1.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(2,2,1)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(1).$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1+{t}^{2})\,+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,k \\  & =2\,i+2t\,j+3{t}^{2}\,k \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =2\,i+2(1)\,j+3(1)^{2}\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to the given curve at the point $P(2,2,1)$ is $2\,i+2\,j+3\,k.$
